sanskrit: vrīḍitā sābhavat sādhvī tadā bharatasattama bhikṣām ādāya viprāya nirjagāma yaśasvinī
english: Ashamed, that noble and glorious woman, O best of the Bharatas, took alms and went out to the brahmin.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca kim idaṃ bhavati tvaṃ māṃ tiṣṭhety uktvā varāṅgane uparodhaṃ kṛtavatī na visarjitavaty asi
english: The brahmin said: What is this, O beautiful lady? You told me to wait, and having kept me waiting, you have not dismissed me. Why?

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca brāhmaṇaṃ krodhasaṃtaptaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā dṛṣṭvā sādhvī manuṣyendra sāntvapūrvaṃ vaco 'bravīt
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Seeing the brahmin burning with anger, blazing as it were with his own fiery energy, that virtuous woman, O lord of men, spoke conciliatory words.

sanskrit: kṣantum arhasi me vipra bhartā me daivataṃ mahat sa cāpi kṣudhitaḥ śrāntaḥ prāptaḥ śuśrūṣito mayā
english: "Please forgive me, O brahmin. My husband is my great deity; he came weary and hungry and I attended to him."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca brāhmaṇā na garīyāṃso garīyāṃs te patiḥ kṛtaḥ gṛhasthadharme vartantī brāhmaṇān avamanyase
english: The brahmin said: Are brahmins not greater? You have made your husband greater than brahmins! Though living in the householder's dharma, you disrespect brahmins.

sanskrit: indro 'py eṣāṃ praṇamate kiṃ punar mānuṣā bhuvi avalipte na jānīṣe vṛddhānāṃ na śrutaṃ tvayā brāhmaṇā hy agnisadṛśā daheyuḥ pṛthivīm api
english: Even Indra bows to them — how much more so ordinary mortals on earth! You are haughty; you do not know, you have not heard the words of the elders. Brahmins, like fire, could burn even the earth itself.

sanskrit: stry uvāca nāvajānāmy ahaṃ viprān devais tulyān manasvinaḥ aparādham imaṃ vipra kṣantum arhasi me 'nagha
english: The woman said: I do not disrespect brahmins, those wise ones who are equal to the gods. Forgive me this offence, O brahmin, O sinless one.

sanskrit: jānāmi tejo viprāṇāṃ mahābhāgyaṃ ca dhīmatām apeyaḥ sāgaraḥ krodhāt kṛto hi lavaṇodakaḥ
english: I know the power of brahmins and the great fortune of those wise ones. The ocean, once undrinkable, was made saline in anger by one of them.

sanskrit: tathaiva dīptatapasāṃ munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām yeṣāṃ krodhāgnir adyāpi daṇḍake nopaśāmyati
english: Likewise the fire of wrath of those sages of blazing austerities and purified souls — that fire does not cool even today in the Daṇḍaka forest.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ paribhavād vātāpiś ca durātmavān agastyam ṛṣim āsādya jīrṇaḥ krūro mahāsuraḥ
english: Because of contempt for brahmins, the wicked and cruel great asura Vātāpi was digested upon encountering the sage Agastya.

sanskrit: prabhāvā bahavaś cāpi śrūyante brahmavādinām krodhaḥ suvipulo brahman prasādaś ca mahātmanām
english: Many such feats of those who speak of Brahman are heard of, O brahmin. Both the wrath and the grace of great souls are immeasurably vast.

sanskrit: asmiṃs tv atikrame brahman kṣantum arhasi me 'nagha patiśuśrūṣayā dharmo yaḥ sa me rocate dvija
english: Yet in this transgression, O sinless brahmin, you should forgive me. The dharma of serving one's husband — that is what appeals to me, O twice-born.

sanskrit: daivateṣv api sarveṣu bhartā me daivataṃ param aviśeṣeṇa tasyāhaṃ kuryāṃ dharmaṃ dvijottama
english: Among all deities, my husband is my supreme deity. Without discrimination I shall perform my duty toward him, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣāyāḥ phalaṃ paśya patyur brāhmaṇa yādṛśam balākā hi tvayā dagdhā roṣāt tad viditaṃ mama
english: See, O brahmin, what fruit comes from devoted service to one's husband — for I know that you burnt the crane in rage.

sanskrit: krodhaḥ śatruḥ śarīrastho manuṣyāṇāṃ dvijottama yaḥ krodhamohau tyajati taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: Anger is the enemy dwelling within the body of men, O best of twice-born. The gods know as a true brahmin the one who abandons anger and delusion.

sanskrit: yo vaded iha satyāni guruṃ saṃtoṣayeta ca hiṃsitaś ca na hiṃseta taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: The one who speaks truth here, who satisfies his teacher, who does not injure though injured — him the gods know as a brahmin.

sanskrit: jitendriyo dharmaparaḥ svādhyāyanirataḥ śuciḥ kāmakrodhau vaśe yasya taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: The one who has conquered the senses, is devoted to dharma, is intent on self-study, is pure, and has desire and anger under control — him the gods know as a brahmin.

sanskrit: yasya cātmasamo loko dharmajñasya manasvinaḥ sarvadharmeṣu ca ratas taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: The one who regards all the world as equal to himself, who knows dharma, who is wise, and who is devoted to all dharmas — him the gods know as a brahmin.

sanskrit: yo 'dhyāpayed adhīyīta yajed vā yājayīta vā dadyād vāpi yathāśakti taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: The one who teaches, studies, sacrifices, officiates at sacrifice, and gives according to his ability — him the gods know as a brahmin.

sanskrit: brahmacārī ca vedānyo adhīyīta dvijottamaḥ svādhyāye cāpramatto vai taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: The twice-born who lives as a student of the Vedas, who studies them and is diligent in self-study — him the gods know as a brahmin.

sanskrit: yad brāhmaṇānāṃ kuśalaṃ tad eṣāṃ parikīrtayet satyaṃ tathā vyāharatāṃ nānṛte ramate manaḥ
english: One should proclaim the good of brahmins and speak truth among them; the mind of those who speak thus takes no delight in falsehood.

sanskrit: dhanaṃ tu brāhmaṇasyāhuḥ svādhyāyaṃ damam ārjavam indriyāṇāṃ nigrahaṃ ca śāśvataṃ dvijasattama satyārjave dharmam āhuḥ paraṃ dharmavido janāḥ
english: The wealth of a brahmin, they say, is self-study, self-restraint, uprightness, and the eternal subduing of the senses, O best of twice-born. Those who know dharma declare truth and uprightness to be the highest dharma.

sanskrit: durjñeyaḥ śāśvato dharmaḥ sa tu satye pratiṣṭhitaḥ śrutipramāṇo dharmaḥ syād iti vṛddhānuśāsanam
english: The eternal dharma is hard to know, yet it is established in truth. Dharma has scripture as its authority — such is the teaching of the elders.

sanskrit: bahudhā dṛśyate dharmaḥ sūkṣma eva dvijottama bhavān api ca dharmajñaḥ svādhyāyanirataḥ śuciḥ na tu tattvena bhagavan dharmān vetsīti me matiḥ
english: Dharma is seen in many forms and is indeed subtle, O best of twice-born. You too are a knower of dharma, devoted to self-study and pure — yet in my opinion, O venerable one, you do not truly know dharmas in their essence.

sanskrit: mātāpitṛbhyāṃ śuśrūṣuḥ satyavādī jitendriyaḥ mithilāyāṃ vasan vyādhaḥ sa te dharmān pravakṣyati tatra gacchasva bhadraṃ te yathākāmaṃ dvijottama
english: A hunter who serves his mother and father, speaks truth, and has his senses under control lives in Mithilā — he will teach you the dharmas. Go there; may it be well with you and may you go as you please, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: atyuktam api me sarvaṃ kṣantum arhasy anindita striyo hy avadhyāḥ sarveṣāṃ ye dharmaviduṣo janāḥ
english: You should forgive whatever excess I may have said, O blameless one, for women are inviolable to all those who know dharma.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca prīto 'smi tava bhadraṃ te gataḥ krodhaś ca śobhane upālambhas tvayā hy ukto mama niḥśreyasaṃ param svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmi sādhayiṣyāmi śobhane
english: The brahmin said: I am pleased with you; may it be well with you, O beautiful one, and my anger is gone. The reproach you gave me is my supreme good. May you be blessed. I shall go and accomplish this, O radiant one.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tayā visṛṣṭo nirgamya svam eva bhavanaṃ yayau vinindan sa dvijo ''tmānaṃ kauśiko narasattama
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Dismissed by her, that brahmin Kauśika went out and returned to his own dwelling, blaming himself, O best of men.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca cintayitvā tad āścaryaṃ striyā proktam aśeṣataḥ vinindan sa dvijo ''tmānam āgaskṛta ivābabhau
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having reflected on that wonder and on all the woman had said, that brahmin, blaming himself, appeared as one who had committed a fault.

sanskrit: cintayānaḥ sa dharmasya sūkṣmāṃ gatim athābravīt śraddadhānena bhāvyaṃ vai gacchāmi mithilām aham
english: Reflecting on the subtle course of dharma he then said: "One must have faith. I shall go to Mithilā."

sanskrit: kṛtātmā dharmavit tasyāṃ vyādho nivasate kila taṃ gacchāmy aham adyaiva dharmaṃ praṣṭuṃ tapodhanam
english: "In that city dwells a hunter who is self-realized and a knower of dharma, they say — a man rich in austerity. I shall go to him this very day to ask about dharma."

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya manasā śraddadhānaḥ striyā vacaḥ balākāpratyayenāsau dharmyaiś ca vacanaiḥ śubhaiḥ saṃpratasthe sa mithilāṃ kautūhalasamanvitaḥ
english: Thus having resolved in his mind, faithful to the woman's words, convinced by the incident of the crane and by her righteous and auspicious words, he set out for Mithilā filled with eager curiosity.

sanskrit: atikrāmann araṇyāni grāmāṃś ca nagarāṇi ca tato jagāma mithilāṃ janakena surakṣitām
english: Passing through forests, villages, and cities, he then came to Mithilā, well protected by Janaka.

sanskrit: dharmasetusamākīrṇāṃ yajñotsavavatīṃ śubhām gopurāṭṭālakavatīṃ gṛhaprākāraśobhitām
english: It was filled with embankments of dharma, filled with sacrifices and festivals, beautiful, graced with towers and gateways, adorned with houses and enclosing walls.

sanskrit: praviśya sa purīṃ ramyāṃ vimānair bahubhir vṛtām paṇyaiś ca bahubhir yuktāṃ suvibhaktamahāpathām
english: Entering that delightful city surrounded by many mansions, well-stocked with many commodities, and with broad well-laid-out streets,

sanskrit: aśvai rathais tathā nāgair yānaiś ca bahubhir vṛtām hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇāṃ nityotsavasamākulām
english: Filled with horses, chariots, elephants, and many vehicles, thronged with cheerful and well-fed people, always bustling with festivity,

sanskrit: so 'paśyad bahuvṛttāntāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ samatikraman dharmavyādham apṛcchac ca sa cāsya kathito dvijaiḥ
english: That brahmin, passing through and seeing all its varied affairs, asked after the righteous hunter, and he was pointed out to him by the brahmins there.

sanskrit: apaśyat tatra gatvā taṃ sūnāmadhye vyavasthitam mārgamāhiṣamāṃsāni vikrīṇantaṃ tapasvinam ākulatvāt tu kretṝṇām ekānte saṃsthito dvijaḥ
english: Going there he saw that austere man stationed in the midst of a meat-market, selling venison and buffalo flesh. Because of the crowd of buyers, the brahmin stood apart to one side.

sanskrit: sa tu jñātvā dvijaṃ prāptaṃ sahasā saṃbhramotthitaḥ ājagāma yato vipraḥ sthita ekānta āsane
english: But the hunter, knowing that the brahmin had arrived, rose up quickly with respect and came to where the brahmin was seated alone.

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca abhivādaye tvā bhagavan svāgataṃ te dvijottama ahaṃ vyādhas tu bhadraṃ te kiṃ karomi praśādhi mām
english: The hunter said: I salute you, O venerable one. Welcome to you, O best of twice-born. I am the hunter — may it be well with you. What shall I do? Command me.

sanskrit: ekapatnyā yad ukto 'si gaccha tvaṃ mithilām iti jānāmy etad ahaṃ sarvaṃ yadarthaṃ tvam ihāgataḥ
english: "I know all of it — that you were told by the devoted wife to go to Mithilā, and the purpose for which you have come here."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca śrutvā tu tasya tad vākyaṃ sa vipro bhṛśaharṣitaḥ dvitīyam idam āścaryam ity acintayata dvijaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Hearing those words of his, that brahmin was greatly delighted. The twice-born reflected: "This is the second wonder."

sanskrit: adeśasthaṃ hi te sthānam iti vyādho 'bravīd dvijam gṛhaṃ gacchāva bhagavan yadi rocayase 'nagha
english: "This place is not a fitting place for you," the hunter told the brahmin. "Let us go home, O venerable one, if it pleases you, O sinless one."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva saṃhṛṣṭo vipro vacanam abravīt agratas tu dvijaṃ kṛtvā sa jagāma gṛhān prati
english: "Very well," the brahmin replied with great joy. Placing the brahmin ahead of him, the hunter went toward his home.

sanskrit: praviśya ca gṛhaṃ ramyam āsanenābhipūjitaḥ pādyam ācamanīyaṃ ca pratigṛhya dvijottamaḥ
english: And entering the pleasant house, the best of twice-born was honored with a seat, and received water for his feet and for rinsing his mouth.

sanskrit: tataḥ sukhopaviṣṭas taṃ vyādhaṃ vacanam abravīt karmaitad vai na sadṛśaṃ bhavataḥ pratibhāti me anutapye bhṛśaṃ tāta tava ghoreṇa karmaṇā
english: Then, seated comfortably, he spoke to the hunter: "This occupation does not seem fitting for you, it appears to me. I am deeply grieved, dear friend, by your dreadful occupation."

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca kulocitam idaṃ karma pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mama vartamānasya me dharme sve manyuṃ mā kṛthā dvija
english: The hunter said: This is the work appropriate to my lineage, inherited from my fathers and forefathers. I live in my own dharma. Do not be angry with me, O twice-born.

sanskrit: dhātrā tu vihitaṃ pūrvaṃ karma svaṃ pālayāmy aham prayatnāc ca gurū vṛddhau śuśrūṣe 'haṃ dvijottama
english: I maintain the occupation ordained by the Creator from the beginning. And I serve with care my parents, the two elders, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: satyaṃ vade nābhyasūye yathāśakti dadāmi ca devatātithibhṛtyānām avaśiṣṭena vartaye
english: I speak truth, I do not slander, I give according to my ability, and I live on what remains after providing for gods, guests, and servants.

sanskrit: na kutsayāmy ahaṃ kiṃ cin na garhe balavattaram kṛtam anveti kartāraṃ purā karma dvijottama
english: I do not revile anything, I do not blame the more powerful. The deed done pursues the doer — that is karma from the past, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyam iha lokasya jīvanam daṇḍanītis trayī vidyā tena lokā bhavanty uta
english: Agriculture, cattle-keeping, and trade are the livelihood of people in this world; also the science of governance and the threefold knowledge of the Vedas — by these the worlds exist.

sanskrit: karma śūdre kṛṣir vaiśye saṃgrāmaḥ kṣatriye smṛtaḥ brahmacaryaṃ tapo mantrāḥ satyaṃ ca brāhmaṇe sadā
english: Service is prescribed for the shudra, agriculture for the vaishya, battle for the kshatriya; celibacy, austerity, sacred chants, and truth always for the brahmin.

sanskrit: rājā praśāsti dharmeṇa svakarmaniratāḥ prajāḥ vikarmāṇaś ca ye ke cit tān yunakti svakarmasu
english: The king governs his subjects in accordance with dharma; those who are devoted to their own duties — and those who transgress their proper duties — he sets back on their own occupations.

sanskrit: bhetavyaṃ hi sadā rājñāṃ prajānām adhipā hi te mārayanti vikarmasthaṃ lubdhā mṛgam iveṣubhiḥ
english: One should always fear kings, for they are lords of their subjects. They slay those who transgress their duties, as hunters with arrows slay their prey.

sanskrit: janakasyeha viprarṣe vikarmastho na vidyate svakarmaniratā varṇāś catvāro 'pi dvijottama
english: In Janaka's realm, O brahmin-sage, there is no one transgressing his duty; all four castes are devoted to their own dharmas, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: sa eṣa janako rājā durvṛttam api cet sutam daṇḍyaṃ daṇḍe nikṣipati tathā na glāti dhārmikam
english: This king Janaka places even a misbehaving son under punishment if he deserves it, and likewise does not neglect the virtuous man.

sanskrit: suyuktacāro nṛpatiḥ sarvaṃ dharmeṇa paśyati śrīś ca rājyaṃ ca daṇḍaś ca kṣatriyāṇāṃ dvijottama
english: The king whose conduct is well ordered sees all things through dharma. Prosperity, sovereignty, and the rod of justice belong to kshatriyas, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: rājāno hi svadharmeṇa śriyam icchanti bhūyasīm sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ trātā rājā bhavaty uta
english: For kings through their own dharma seek abundant prosperity, and the king indeed becomes the protector of all the castes.

sanskrit: pareṇa hi hatān brahman varāhamahiṣān aham na svayaṃ hanmi viprarṣe vikrīṇāmi sadā tv aham
english: O brahmin, I do not myself slay the boars and buffaloes — they are killed by others, O brahmin-sage. I only sell them always.

sanskrit: na bhakṣayāmi māṃsāni ṛtugāmī tathā hy aham sadopavāsī ca tathā naktabhojī tathā dvija
english: I do not eat meat; I approach my wife only in her season. I am always fasting and I eat only at night, O twice-born.

sanskrit: aśīlaś cāpi puruṣo bhūtvā bhavati śīlavān prāṇihiṃsārataś cāpi bhavate dhārmikaḥ punaḥ
english: Even a man who has been of bad character can become virtuous; and even one addicted to harming living beings can again become righteous.

sanskrit: vyabhicārān narendrāṇāṃ dharmaḥ saṃkīryate mahān adharmo vardhate cāpi saṃkīryante tathā prajāḥ
english: Through the transgressions of kings, great dharma becomes confused, adharma increases, and likewise the subjects intermingle.

sanskrit: uruṇḍā vāmanāḥ kubjāḥ sthūlaśīrṣās tathaiva ca klībāś cāndhāś ca jāyante badhirā lambacūcukāḥ pārthivānām adharmatvāt prajānām abhavaḥ sadā
english: Dwarfs, hunchbacks, those with large heads, eunuchs, the blind, the deaf, and those with hanging ears are born — from the unrighteousness of kings the decline of subjects always follows.

sanskrit: sa eṣa rājā janakaḥ sarvaṃ dharmeṇa paśyati anugṛhṇan prajāḥ sarvāḥ svadharmaniratāḥ sadā
english: This king Janaka sees all things through dharma, always favoring his subjects who are each devoted to their own dharma.

sanskrit: ye caiva māṃ praśaṃsanti ye ca nindanti mānavāḥ sarvān supariṇītena karmaṇā toṣayāmy aham
english: Both those who praise me and those who blame me — I satisfy all people through well-measured conduct.

sanskrit: ye jīvanti svadharmeṇa saṃbhuñjante ca pārthivāḥ na kiṃ cid upajīvanti dakṣā utthānaśīlinaḥ
english: Those who live by their own dharma and those kings who enjoy accordingly — those who are capable and diligent do not depend on anyone for their livelihood.

sanskrit: śaktyānnadānaṃ satataṃ titikṣā dharmanityatā yathārhaṃ pratipūjā ca sarvabhūteṣu vai dayā tyāgān nānyatra martyānāṃ guṇās tiṣṭhanti pūruṣe
english: Constant giving of food according to one's ability, forbearance, steadfastness in dharma, honor given as befits each person, and compassion toward all beings — virtues of mortals rest nowhere in a person except through generosity.

sanskrit: mṛṣāvādaṃ pariharet kuryāt priyam ayācitaḥ na ca kāmān na saṃrambhān na dveṣād dharmam utsṛjet
english: One should shun false speech, should do what is pleasing without being asked, and should not abandon dharma out of desire, anger, or hatred.

sanskrit: priye nātibhṛśaṃ hṛṣyed apriye na ca saṃjvaret na muhyed arthakṛcchreṣu na ca dharmaṃ parityajet
english: One should not be excessively overjoyed at the pleasant nor burn in distress at the unpleasant; one should not be bewildered in financial difficulties, nor should one abandon dharma.

sanskrit: karma cet kiṃ cid anyat syād itaran na samācaret yat kalyāṇam abhidhyāyet tatrātmānaṃ niyojayet
english: If there is some other better course of action, one should not practice what is different from it. Whatever is auspicious — on that should one fix oneself.

sanskrit: na pāpaṃ prati pāpaḥ syāt sādhur eva sadā bhavet ātmanaiva hataḥ pāpo yaḥ pāpaṃ kartum icchati
english: One should not be wicked in return for wickedness; one should always be a good person. The wicked one who wishes to do evil is slain by his own self.

sanskrit: karma caitad asādhūnāṃ vṛjinānām asādhuvat na dharmo 'stīti manvānāḥ śucīn avahasanti ye aśraddadhānā dharmasya te naśyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: This is the conduct of the wicked, of sinners acting wickedly — those who think there is no dharma and who mock the pure. Those without faith in dharma perish — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: mahādṛtir ivādhmātaḥ pāpo bhavati nityadā mūḍhānām avaliptānām asāraṃ bhāṣitaṃ bhavet darśayaty antarātmānaṃ divā rūpam ivāṃśumān
english: The wicked man is always puffed up like a great inflated water-skin; the speech of the foolish and arrogant is without substance. He reveals his inner self like the sun reveals its form by day.

sanskrit: na loke rājate mūrkhaḥ kevalātmapraśaṃsayā api ceha mṛjā hīnaḥ kṛtavidyaḥ prakāśate
english: A fool does not shine in the world by self-praise alone; even one who is without physical grace but has acquired learning shines forth.

sanskrit: abruvan kasya cin nindām ātmapūjām avarṇayan na kaś cid guṇasaṃpannaḥ prakāśo bhuvi dṛśyate
english: Not speaking ill of anyone, not lauding oneself — no one who is endowed with virtues is seen to be prominently visible on the earth.

sanskrit: vikarmaṇā tapyamānaḥ pāpād viparimucyate naitat kuryāṃ punar iti dvitīyāt parimucyate
english: One who is tormented by wrongful action is freed from sin; resolving "I will not do this again," one is freed from the second offence.

sanskrit: karmaṇā yena teneha pāpād dvijavarottama evaṃ śrutir iyaṃ brahman dharmeṣu paridṛśyate
english: By whatever action one is freed here from sin, O best of twice-born — thus, O brahmin, this teaching is seen throughout the dharma scriptures.

sanskrit: pāpāny abuddhveha purā kṛtāni; prāg dharmaśīlo vinihanti paścāt dharmo brahman nudate pūruṣāṇāṃ; yat kurvate pāpam iha pramādāt
english: Sins formerly committed here in ignorance — one of virtuous character destroys them afterward. O brahmin, dharma drives away from men that which they do in sin and negligence here.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ kṛtvā hi manyeta nāham asmīti pūruṣaḥ cikīrṣed eva kalyāṇaṃ śraddadhāno 'nasūyakaḥ
english: Having done wrong, a person should think "I am not that self" and should only desire to do good, being faithful and free from malice.

sanskrit: vasanasyeva chidrāṇi sādhūnāṃ vivṛṇoti yaḥ pāpaṃ cet puruṣaḥ kṛtvā kalyāṇam abhipadyate mucyate sarvapāpebhyo mahābhrair iva candramāḥ
english: He who exposes the faults of the virtuous as one exposes the holes in a garment — if such a person, having done evil, turns toward the good, he is freed from all sins, as the moon is freed from great clouds.
